explanations: luna: The section develops sky and earth as a structure scene; this verse calls the sky a “بِنَاءً” above an earth made a resting spread (“فِرَاشًا”), giving that architectural pairing a related formulation. | terra: God makes the earth a bed and ٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءً, a built canopy; the paired ground and building anticipate the section's placed and raised creation forms.

luna: The section names the dictionary extension from undoing a built tie to breaking a covenant; this verse describes people who “يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ,” matching that extension directly. | terra: Those who يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ ٱللَّهِ after its binding give the covenant use of dismantling that the source derives from rope and building.

luna: This verse says the Mount was raised above the people (“رَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ”), a concrete instance of the section’s root ر ف ع applied to a physical object. | terra: God رَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ, lifting the mountain over the covenant community; a massive placed object becomes suspended overhead.

luna: This verse again stages the Mount raised above the people (“رَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ”), repeating the physical-object sense that the section distinguishes from raised remembrance. | terra: The mountain is again raised over the people at covenant-taking, pairing physical elevation with a bond they are commanded to hold firmly.
terra: God makes the House a recurring destination and security and names Abraham's station as a place of prayer; it clarifies the placed House as an appointed human locus.

luna: The section’s root ر ف ع is explicitly used of raising a structure; this verse has Abraham and Ishmael raise the House’s foundations (“يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ”) while asking their Lord to accept their work. | terra: Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations while addressing their Lord; the act gives the section's رَفَعَ its literal architectural scene and joins building to prayer.
terra: مَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ reverses the section's رغبة “toward” the Lord by using the same stance “away from” Abraham's way; Abraham is also the builder in 2:127.

luna: The section develops the hardship/ease pairing; this verse states that God wants ease and not hardship (“يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ”), making the opposition explicit. | terra: God wills ٱلْيُسْرَ for people and does not will ٱلْعُسْرَ; the explicit opposition clarifies the two poles compressed into the section's assurance.

terra: The ayah asks about ٱلْمَيْسِرِ, a game of chance, and weighs its benefit against its great harm; it plausibly echoes the source dictionary's unusual use of “hardship” for a peg game, though it is not the same game.

luna: The section’s dictionary form الْعَقْد is a knot that can be undone; this verse uses the matching form “عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ” for the marriage tie and sets a boundary on when it may be contracted.

luna: The section’s dictionary form الْعَقْد is a knot and its extension to a bond; this verse names “عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ” in a divorce settlement, showing the marriage tie as a held bond in the very setting where it may be released.
terra: وَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ commands believers to stand devoutly for God, a direct bodily and devotional gloss on the section's “stand erect.”
terra: God raises some messengers دَرَجَٰتٍ; prophetic distinction is expressed through the same vertical verb used for the section's elevated name.
terra: The believer grasps ٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَا, the firmest handhold that cannot break; it supplies the securely bound opposite of an unravelled rope.
terra: A town lies خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا, then bones are raised and clothed with flesh; collapsed architecture and bodily reconstruction meet in the same demonstration.

luna: The section’s root ع س ر is paired with ease; this verse makes that transition concrete for a debtor, “ذُو عُسْرَةٍ” receiving respite until “مَيْسَرَةٍ,” a particular burden eased in its own context.

luna: The section depicts a load pressing on a back and then being removed; this prayer asks God not to make the community carry a burden (“وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا إِصْرًا”), a specific appeal at the imposition side of that bodily image. | terra: The prayer asks the Lord not to lay on believers an iṣr or load beyond their capacity; it makes relief from an unbearable burden an explicit supplication.

luna: The section labels root وَضْع as setting down; Mary’s “وَضَعَتْهَا” here is the distinct dictionary branch for delivering a child. The bodily release may illuminate a burden being put down, though that bridge is not explicit in the section.

luna: The section’s root ر ف ع is lifting from one’s resting place; here God tells Jesus “وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ,” another specific raising of a person. | terra: God tells Jesus إِنِّى ... رَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ, moving a person toward God rather than raising an object or a name; it marks a distinct Quranic sense of the same root.

luna: The section contrasts the House’s being placed with its foundations being raised; this verse says the first House for people was “وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ” at Bakkah, giving the same sanctuary the placed state paired with 2:127. | terra: The first House is described as وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ; this is the same House whose foundations are raised in 2:127, so placement and elevation become two states of one structure.

luna: The section’s yarn and covenant images turn on a bond being undone; this verse’s rope of God is to be held together (“وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا”), a specific image of binding cohesion against unraveling. | terra: وَٱعْتَصِمُوا۟ بِحَبْلِ ٱللَّهِ asks the community to hold fast together to God's rope and not divide, the communal opposite of strong thread deliberately unravelled.
terra: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ states God's intent to lighten human beings because they were created weak, matching the direction of the removed load.

luna: This verse says the Mount was raised over them (“وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ الطُّورَ”), another specific physical elevation under the covenant scene. | terra: God raises the mountain above them بِمِيثَٰقِهِمْ; elevated mass and covenant firmness meet in one clause.

luna: This verse names the breaking of a firm covenant (“نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَاقَهُمْ”), another direct use of the section’s root extension from undoing a built tie to breaking a pledge. | terra: فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَٰقَهُمْ names Israel's breaking of covenant as a cause of judgment, another contextual instance of the physical verb transferred to a bond.

luna: This verse states of Jesus, “بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ,” a second Quranic formulation of the bodily raising relevant to the section’s raised-object sense. | terra: بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ reiterates Jesus's raising to God, a personal elevation that lies between physical lifting and bestowed honor.

luna: The section’s root ن ص ب dictionary sense includes setting a stone upright; this verse refers to what is sacrificed upon “النُّصُبِ,” erected cult stones. That is a different religious use of the same set-up-stone branch, marking a boundary from the section’s upright stance. | terra: Sacrifice عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ and division by arrows place an erected stone and lots in one scene, concretizing the section's secondary game-and-peg field.
terra: بِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَٰقَهُمْ again treats covenant-breaking as unmaking something secured, with hardening of hearts as its consequence.

luna: The section’s dictionary form الْعَقْد names a knot and its extension to covenants; this verse speaks of “عَقَّدتُّمُ الْأَيْمَانَ,” bound oaths, putting the section’s knot-and-oath link into a specific Quranic formulation.

luna: The section’s root ن ص ب dictionary sense includes setting a stone upright; this verse names “الْأَنْصَابَ,” cult stones, among things forbidden. It shows the same erected-stone branch in a distinct context from the section’s command to stand. | terra: ٱلْمَيْسِرُ وَٱلْأَنصَابُ وَٱلْأَزْلَٰمُ places gaming, erected cult-stones from ن ص ب, and lots together; it strongly recalls the source dictionary's game of a set-up peg struck by another piece.
terra: The gaming and lots of 5:90 obstruct remembrance of God and prayer; the erected-game scene therefore stands opposite the section's command to turn exertion toward the Lord.

terra: Game reached by hands and رِمَاحُكُمْ supplies a Quranic spear scene for the source dictionary's two examples—the erected spear and the spear's ṣadr as its top—but the ayah does not itself erect the spear.

luna: The section’s load is removed from the back; this verse depicts people carrying their burdens “عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِمْ,” the same body-and-load scene under the opposite condition. | terra: The losers carry أَوْزَارَهُمْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِمْ, their burdens upon their backs; this is the clearest external scene for the load that makes the back creak in the section.

luna: The section’s root ر ف ع includes elevation; this verse says God raises degrees whom He wills (“نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَاءُ”), applying the same elevation to rank rather than a building or name. | terra: نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ converts upward constructional motion into degrees of wisdom and favor.

luna: The section names root ص د ر through the chest in 94:1; here guidance opens the chest toward Islam while misguidance makes it narrow and constricted, a specific opening/boundary that clarifies the bodily image. | terra: God opens a person's chest to submission, but makes another chest tight and constricted كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ; chest-opening and difficult upward motion meet in a single contrast.
terra: لَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ sets a boundary on load-bearing: another soul does not take over one's burden, whereas the section attributes relief directly to God.

luna: This verse says God raised some people above others in degrees (“وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ”), a specific status-elevation parallel to raised remembrance. | terra: God raises some people فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَٰتٍ for a test; the ayah adds hierarchy and responsibility to the image of elevation.
terra: The Prophet is told not to let there be حَرَجٌ in his chest because of the revealed Book, another divine address relieving prophetic constriction.
terra: Thamud carve houses from mountains after being settled in the land; erected dwelling is cut directly out of a fixed natural mass.
terra: When the plague is removed until an appointed term, Pharaoh's people immediately يَنكُثُونَ, undoing their promise like a loosened bond.

luna: The section’s root gloss وَضْع is setting something down; this verse says the Messenger “يَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ” (removes their burden) and their shackles, directly pairing the image of a load put aside with release from burdens. | terra: The messenger يَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَٱلْأَغْلَٰلَ removes peoples' load and fetters; it closely parallels the divine removal of the addressee's burden in 94:2.

luna: This verse depicts the mountain lifted over the people like a canopy and feared to fall; the suspended mountain makes elevation and threatened collapse visible together, as in the section’s raised and cracking structures. | terra: The mountain is wrenched over them كَأَنَّهُۥ ظُلَّةٌ, like a canopy; without using رفع, it restages the raised-overhead structure during covenant-taking.

luna: This verse says that, had God willed, He would have raised the person by the signs (“لَرَفَعْنَاهُ بِهَا”), but he clung to earth; that stated alternative gives a specific rise/low attachment boundary to the section’s elevation motif. | terra: God says He could have raised the man by the signs, but he أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ; possible elevation is reversed by clinging to the low ground.

luna: The section connects dismantling a tie with breach of covenant; this verse describes people who break their covenant repeatedly (“يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ”), adding repetition to the same act. | terra: The repeatedly faithless ثُمَّ يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَهُمْ فِى كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ show a bond continually dismantled rather than held firm.

luna: The section’s oath and covenant examples describe a pledge being broken; here opponents break their oaths after their covenant (“نَّكَثُوا أَيْمَانَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ”), the same breach in a distinct treaty context. | terra: فَإِن نَّكَثُوٓا۟ أَيْمَٰنَهُم uses the related image of untying or breaking oaths; it is a nonlexical parallel to نقض a tightened covenant.
terra: The people نَّكَثُوا۟ أَيْمَٰنَهُمْ and tried to expel the messenger, giving the oath-untying image a concrete act of betrayal.
terra: The faithful formulation إِنَّآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ رَٰغِبُونَ reproduces the section's directed desire toward God almost word for word.
terra: Those who take a mosque for harm and division make a religious building serve rupture; 9:108–109 answer it with foundations of reverence and a collapsing bank.
terra: A mosque founded عَلَى ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ supplies the stable foundation against which 9:109's collapsing building is judged.

luna: The section treats a sound build undone as an image of collapse; this verse contrasts a foundation on devotion with a building on an eroding bank that collapses with its builder (“فَانْهَارَ بِهِ”), making the stability boundary explicit. | terra: One building is founded on reverence, while another stands on a collapsing bank and falls with its builder; the ayah turns construction and structural failure into a moral comparison.
terra: Their building remains a doubt in their hearts إِلَّآ أَن تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ; the built structure persists until the builders' own inner bodies are cut apart.
terra: Thirst, نَصَبٌ, and hunger suffered in God's path are credited as righteous action; this uses the section's nasb family in the fatigue sense of strenuous service.
terra: The possibility that the Prophet's chest becomes constricted by objections to revelation supplies a specific pressure from which divine chest-opening relieves him.

luna: This verse uses “نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَاءُ” for elevation in rank; it gives the section’s raising image a personal and social, rather than architectural, instance. | terra: نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ follows Joseph's discerning stratagem, another use of elevation for granted rank rather than moved matter.
terra: Joseph وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ, physically seating his parents above on the throne; elevation becomes both spatial and honorific.

luna: The section’s root ر ف ع means lifting a set object and also raising a building; this verse applies the same action to the heavens, “رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا,” shifting the lift from body and remembrance to cosmic structure. | terra: God رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا; the heavens are a raised structure whose visible supports are absent.

luna: The section cites 13:2 for the raised heavens; this next ayah turns to the earth spread out, mountains made firm, and rivers, extending the same ordered sky-and-earth scene. Its contribution is the ground below the raised sky. | terra: God extends the earth and makes in it firm mountains, another direct pairing of horizontal expanse and fixed elevation.

luna: The section’s root extension is covenant-breaking; this verse describes the opposite boundary, people who fulfill God’s covenant and “لَا يَنقُضُونَ الْمِيثَاقَ.” | terra: Those who fulfil God's covenant وَلَا يَنقُضُونَ ٱلْمِيثَٰقَ embody the positive boundary: a bond is kept from the unmaking named by the section.

luna: This verse repeats the section’s direct covenant-breaking image and adds cutting what God commanded to be joined; that severed bond makes the undoing concrete beyond the covenant itself. | terra: Those who يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مِيثَٰقِهِ repeat the section's transfer of physical dismantling to a covenant made firm.
terra: The good word is a tree أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ; rooted stability and upward reach give a living analogue for a name raised on a firm base.
terra: The bad word is a tree ٱجْتُثَّتْ مِن فَوْقِ ٱلْأَرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ, uprooted with no stability; it reverses the section's erected and securely tied forms.

luna: The section’s 88:19–20 scene links erected mountains with the earth; this verse likewise joins earth spread out and mountains cast into it (“وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَاهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ”). | terra: God spreads the earth and casts firm mountains into it; horizontal preparation and installed masses repeat the section's construction grammar.
terra: Paradise's inhabitants are untouched by نَصَبٌ and never expelled, setting restful permanence against the toil sense latent in فَٱنصَبْ.
terra: They carve houses from mountains while feeling secure, making architectural firmness the setting for a security that proves temporary.
terra: God knows the Prophet's chest يَضِيقُ because of what people say; 15:98 answers that constriction with directed worship, paralleling opened chest followed by exertion toward the Lord.

terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ commands the chest-constricted Prophet to glorify his Lord and assume a worship posture, closely matching the section's final two imperatives.
terra: God casts firm mountains into earth lest it sway with people, giving the erected forms a stabilizing structural function.
terra: Misleaders carry their own burdens and some burdens of those they mislead; it extends the bodily load image from one carrier to compounded moral responsibility.

luna: The section’s dictionary form نَقَضَ includes dismantling a solidly built structure; here a building is attacked from its foundations and its roof falls on its people, a concrete collapse that gives the section’s cracking-structure image an external counterpart. | terra: God comes at their building مِنَ ٱلْقَوَاعِدِ and the roof falls on them; foundations raised in 2:127 here become the point from which a structure is undone.

luna: The section cites oath-breaking as a form of undoing; this preceding verse explicitly forbids breaking oaths after making them firm (“وَلَا تَنقُضُوا الْأَيْمَانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا”). The next ayah, 16:92, supplies the yarn image; this row states the oath’s own contribution. | terra: لَا تَنقُضُوا۟ ٱلْأَيْمَٰنَ forbids dismantling oaths after confirming them; 16:92 then makes this abstract breach visible as untwisted yarn.

luna: The section’s dictionary form نَقَضَ covers undoing a firmly made rope; this verse stages a woman unraveling her spun yarn after it was strong (“نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ”), the section’s clearest counter-image to the back under strain. | terra: The woman who نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا after making it strong supplies the section's literal thread-unravelling scene and explains how the same act images broken oaths.

luna: The section connects the undoing of a firm tie to breaking oaths; this continuation warns against using oaths deceptively and describes a foot slipping after it was firmly set. 16:91–92 state the oath and yarn images; this ayah adds the consequence of instability.
terra: مَن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا uses an opened chest for willing unbelief; it is the moral reversal that shows chest-opening is not automatically relief or guidance.
terra: The repeated rule that no bearer bears another's burden distinguishes divine removal of a burden from transferring it to a second human carrier.

luna: The section’s command to stand is followed by turning toward the Lord and by raised remembrance; this verse commands the Prophet’s night vigil and connects it to the Lord’s promise of a praised station, joining devotional stance with elevation. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to night prayer so that his Lord may raise him مَقَامًا مَّحْمُودًا; exertion culminates in an elevated, praised station.
terra: On the Day the mountains are moved and the earth appears bare; it reverses the installed mountains and laid-out earth of the creation tableau.
terra: Moses says لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًا; journey-fatigue supplies a clear Quranic instance of the root's non-erection sense.
terra: Moses asks not to be burdened مِنْ أَمْرِى عُسْرًا; hardship is pictured as something imposed on an affair, joining the section's burden and difficulty fields.

luna: The section describes a load making the back sound as if a structure were cracking and gives building erection as a dictionary sense; here a wall is on the verge of collapse and Khidr restores it (“فَأَقَامَهُ”), a specific reversal from failing structure to upright structure. | terra: Moses's companion straightens a wall يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ, “wanting to collapse”; it is the most exact scene of a built thing at the instant before disassembly.
terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn promises to speak to the righteous مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا, making ease the mode of just rule.

terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn asks the people to help him بِقُوَّةٍ so he may make a barrier between them and their enemies; this states the cooperative force and protective purpose behind the construction in 18:96.
terra: Iron blocks are raised until the gap's two sides are level and molten metal is poured over them; this is a detailed scene of erecting and consolidating a structure.
terra: The completed barrier cannot be climbed or pierced, supplying the moment of structural firmness before its promised levelling in 18:98.
terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn says his Lord will make the firm barrier دَكَّآءَ when the promise comes; even the tightly constructed work is ultimately dismantled by its Lord.
terra: God grants Abraham and his kin لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا, a lofty true renown; this is the closest nonlexical formulation of raising a person's remembrance.

luna: The section’s root ر ف ع includes physically lifting an object; this verse says Idris was raised to a high place (“وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا”), a direct instance of that action. | terra: وَرَفَعْنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا places Idris in a high station, combining the root with explicit height.
terra: The heavens nearly rupture, earth splits, and mountains collapse under a monstrous claim; speech itself places creation's built forms on the brink of structural failure.
terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ says revelation was made easy in the Prophet's tongue, linking ease, prophetic speech, and the tongue released in Moses's prayer.

luna: Moses’s “رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي” directly repeats the section’s chest-opening image. The linked 20:27 adds the request to untie his tongue’s knot; this ayah contributes the chest-opening side of that paired prayer. | terra: Moses prays رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى; the exact chest-opening phrase places the section's opened chest beside the prayer whose tongue-knot is loosened in 20:27.
terra: Moses asks وَيَسِّرْ لِى أَمْرِى between opening his chest and loosening his tongue-knot, bringing ease into the same sequence of relief that the section develops.

luna: The section’s dictionary form الْعُقْدَة is a knot and it distinguishes a knot loosened for rescue from yarn destructively unraveled; Moses asks, “وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي,” a direct speech-knot release. | terra: Moses asks his Lord to loosen عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى; unlike destructive unravelling, releasing this knot enables speech and so marks the section's positive form of undoing.

luna: In the linked 20:27 prayer, Moses asks that a knot be untied from his tongue; this next ayah states the release’s purpose, that people understand his speech (“يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي”). | terra: يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى states the enabling result of the loosened tongue-knot in 20:27, distinguishing liberating release from destructive unravelling.
terra: Immediately after asking for chest-opening and a loosened knot, Moses asks his Lord for a وَزِيرًا from his family; the helper stands against a solitary bearer crushed by his load.
terra: Moses asks ٱشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِى, “strengthen my back through him”; this directly reverses the section's back weakened to the point of creaking under a burden.
terra: وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى gives the purpose of the strengthened back in 20:31: the entrusted affair will be shared rather than borne alone.
luna: The section describes earth as placed for living beings; this verse calls it a cradle made for its addressees (“جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا”), specifying the earth’s supporting role.
terra: Whoever turns from the reminder يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وِزْرًا, carrying a burden on resurrection, supplies another explicit moral load.
terra: The burden carried in 20:100 persists, and the ayah calls it an evil load on resurrection; it supplies the crushing duration and valuation of that burden.
terra: God says He will scatter the mountains completely; 20:106–107 show the result as a level surface without relief, undoing the scene in which mountains are erected.
terra: The removed mountains leave the earth قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا, a level open expanse; the protruding forms of the section's nasb image have disappeared.
terra: لَا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَآ أَمْتًا denies both hollow and rise in the level earth, explicitly marking the boundary of the erected-form image.
terra: The revealed Book contains ذِكْرُكُمْ, which can mean the audience's reminder or honor; this is a plausible communal counterpart to an elevated personal dhikr.
terra: The heavens and earth were رَتْقًا, sewn or closed together, before God فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا, split them apart; creation itself begins with the opening of a joined structure.
terra: Firm mountains are placed in the earth so it will not shake with its inhabitants, another explicit act of stabilizing installation.
terra: The sky is made سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا, a protected roof, giving architectural force to the section's description of the heavens as raised construction.
terra: وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ places just scales at resurrection, repeating the exact placement of balance in 55:7 and making placement serve measured order.
terra: Abraham makes the idols جُذَٰذًا, shattered pieces, except their largest; objects of cultic erection are physically dismantled.
terra: The prophets call on God رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا and humble themselves; desire becomes sustained devotional action directed to Him.
terra: God will roll up the sky كَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ; the raised canopy is deliberately folded away like a written scroll.
terra: On the Hour, every pregnant female تَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا; birth is literally “laying down” a carried load, an embodied secondary sense of وضع.

terra: The frustrated person is told to extend a rope to ٱلسَّمَآءِ and cut it; this plausibly joins a cord to an overhead support and severing, though whether “sky” means a ceiling in the scene is interpretively uncertain.

luna: The section’s House passage pairs its placement for people with raised foundations; this verse identifies the House’s assigned place for Abraham (“بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَاهِيمَ مَكَانَ الْبَيْتِ”), adding the site to that same sanctuary scene. | terra: God assigns Abraham مَكَانَ ٱلْبَيْتِ and orders the House purified for circumambulators and those standing, bowing, and prostrating; place, building, Lord-directed worship, and upright posture converge.
terra: Destroyed settlements lie خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا, fallen upon their roofs, beside an abandoned well and lofty palace; built height and ruin share one landscape.
terra: God holds the sky أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ; the raised canopy is actively kept from falling onto the placed earth, marking the stability boundary of the construction image.
terra: God forms bones, clothes them with flesh, and produces another creation; the body is assembled stage by stage rather than allowed to come apart.

luna: The section’s root gloss ر ف ع includes raising a building and pairs it with raised remembrance; this verse joins both: houses are permitted “أَن تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ,” making construction and remembrance one scene. | terra: Houses God permits to be raised, فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ, are also where His name is remembered; one ayah thus joins the section's raised building to raised remembrance.
terra: The people within the raised houses of 24:36 are not distracted from God's remembrance and prayer; this supplies the enacted dhikr for which those houses are elevated.
terra: The sky is split open with clouds and angels descend, presenting a breach in the raised canopy rather than its stable elevation.
terra: God gives Moses the Book and makes his brother Aaron a وَزِيرًا with him, supplying the divinely granted helper associated with bearing and supporting a weighty task.
terra: Servants of the Merciful spend the night لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَٰمًا, prostrate and standing for their Lord, enacting the posture and direction of the final commands.

luna: Moses says his chest constricts and his tongue does not flow (“وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِي”); this gives a concrete blocked state against the section’s chest-opening and the knot-loosening prayer in 20:27. | terra: Moses says his chest constricts and his tongue does not proceed freely; this joins the two impairments answered by the prayer of 20:25–27.
terra: Abraham asks for لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ, truthful mention among later generations, furnishing the prayer-side counterpart to God raising a name.
terra: Thamud carve skillful houses from mountains, another repeated scene of shaping the massive erected form into built shelter.
terra: God promises Moses سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ, strengthening his arm through his brother; bodily support counters the image of a body failing beneath its work.
terra: The misleaders will carry أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالًا مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ, loads piled with further loads, intensifying the section's strained-carrier image.

luna: The section’s dictionary entry for root ن ق ض concerns undoing what was made solidly; this verse calls the spider’s house the weakest of houses. The contrast between firm construction and a deliberately fragile dwelling is specific, though the verse does not depict it being dismantled. | terra: The spider's house is called أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ, the frailest of houses; it is a built form whose weakness makes misplaced reliance visible.
terra: The sky and earth تَقُومَانِ بِأَمْرِهِ, stand by God's command; cosmic stability is expressed as sustained uprightness.

luna: This verse joins heavens made without visible pillars to mountains cast into the earth; it repeats the section’s two specific creation images of supported sky and set mountains, even though it uses different verbs. | terra: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا repeats the unsupported-heavens image and then says mountains were cast into earth to stabilize it.
terra: One who turns his face to God while doing good has grasped ٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ; firm attachment is joined to the same directed stance toward the Lord as 94:8.
terra: God and His angels bless the Prophet and believers are commanded to bless him, providing an enacted, continually repeated form of his elevated remembrance.
terra: The heavens, earth, and mountains refuse to carry the trust, but the human carries it; the ayah stages a moral weight against both cosmic structures and the human bearer.
terra: Solomon's body remains standing on a staff until the staff is eaten and he falls; the bodily structure is held erect, then gives way when its support is removed.

luna: The section says remembrance is raised; here good speech ascends to God and righteous action raises it (“الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ يَصْعَدُ إِلَيْهِ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ”), a close parallel for elevated mention through words. | terra: إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ makes good speech ascend to God and says righteous work raises it; verbal remembrance acquires the upward motion of the section's construction verb.
terra: No female carries or تَضَعُ except with God's knowledge; the birth sense preserves the movement from bodily load to setting it down.
terra: Even when a heavily laden soul calls someone إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا, none of it is carried for them; this is the fullest boundary-scene around the section's released load.
terra: In the lasting abode, لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ; absence of fatigue bounds the exertion commanded in the present life.
terra: God holds the heavens and earth أَن تَزُولَا, lest they cease or slip away; maintained cosmic structure is the opposite of a form coming undone.
terra: The objector presents decayed bones and asks who can revive them, posing bodily disassembly as a challenge answered in 36:79.
terra: God who produced the bones the first time will revive them, establishing divine reconstruction after complete bodily decay.
terra: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ says God left Noah an enduring mention among later people, a concrete form of preserved and elevated remembrance.
terra: Abraham turns upon the idols, striking them with his right hand, another concrete undoing of standing cult objects.

terra: The people command one another to build a structure for Abraham and cast him into its fire; human construction is turned into an instrument of destruction against the future raiser of the House's foundations.
terra: God leaves Abraham's mention among later generations, directly answering Abraham's request in 26:84 for truthful later renown.
terra: God leaves Moses and Aaron an enduring mention among later people, repeating the form of divinely preserved reputation.
terra: God leaves Elias an enduring mention among later people, another repeated realization of remembrance carried beyond a prophet's lifetime.
terra: Pharaoh is called ذُو ٱلْأَوْتَادِ, possessor of stakes; the object directly recalls the source dictionary's erected wooden peg.
terra: Job says Satan touched him بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ, using the same root for affliction or exhaustion rather than an erected object.
terra: No bearer bears another's burden, so the section's “We laid down from you” remains an act of divine relief rather than ordinary substitution.
terra: The night worshipper is prostrate and standing, wary of the hereafter and hoping for his Lord's mercy; upright exertion is explicitly directed by fear and desire toward the Lord.
terra: Believers receive chambers with further chambers built above them, a literal structure articulated through vertical layering.

luna: The section names root ص د ر through an opened chest; this verse describes a chest opened to Islam and contrasts it with hard hearts, giving the image a spiritual opening and its boundary. | terra: One whose chest God has opened to submission stands in light from his Lord, an explicit parallel to the divinely opened chest in the surah.
terra: The earth is wholly in God's grasp and the heavens are folded in His right hand, a final reversal of the spread earth and raised sky.

luna: The divine epithet “رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ” names the raiser of degrees; it connects the section’s raised-height vocabulary to exalted rank in a verse about revelation. | terra: رَفِيعُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتِ describes God as exalted in degrees or raiser of ranks, extending the elevation field from structures and servants to the Lord's own majesty.

luna: This verse pairs earth made a settled place with sky as a structure (“الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً”), a direct variant of the section’s earth-and-raised-sky construction scene. | terra: God makes the earth a settled place and ٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءً, then fashions human forms well; cosmic building and bodily construction meet in one ayah.
terra: God places firm mountains above the earth and apportions its provisions, joining installed structure to measured provision.
terra: وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنثَىٰ وَلَا تَضَعُ repeats carrying and laying down in pregnancy, a concrete semantic bridge between load and placement.
terra: تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِن فَوْقِهِنَّ depicts the heavens nearly splitting from above, while angels glorify their Lord, joining threatened structure to the رب stance.
terra: God sends down the Book with truth and the balance, paralleling 55:7's placed measure and tying cosmic order to revealed judgment.

luna: This verse describes some being raised above others in degrees (“وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ”), a specific figurative counterpart to raised mention. | terra: God says وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَٰتٍ in distributing livelihoods, mapping the raised/lower spatial image onto social arrangement.
terra: The revelation is ذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ, remembrance or honor for the prophetic addressee and his people; it clarifies what an elevated dhikr can mean.
terra: After punishment is removed from them, إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ; relief is answered by breaking the pledged response.
terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ repeats that the revelation is eased on the prophetic tongue so people may remember.
terra: حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا uniquely joins the section's two terms: war “lays down” its burdens, turning relief from a load into an enacted image.
terra: فَمَن نَّكَثَ فَإِنَّمَا يَنكُثُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ treats breaking a pledge as untying it against oneself, close to the section's rope-derived covenant metaphor.
terra: Believers may not تَرْفَعُوا۟ أَصْوَٰتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِىِّ; human voices are forbidden to elevate themselves over the Prophet whose remembrance God raises.
terra: Those who lower their voices before God's messenger are praised, completing 49:2's prohibition and setting human self-lowering beside God's elevation of the Prophet's remembrance.

luna: The section cites 50:7 for earth spread and mountains cast into it; this preceding ayah asks readers to look at the sky above and how it was built and adorned, completing the same constructed-sky/ground scene. | terra: The audience is asked how God بَنَيْنَٰهَا وَزَيَّنَّٰهَا and left the sky without fissures; it presents creation as an intact overhead building.

luna: This repeated earth-and-mountains scene also says the earth is spread and firm mountains cast into it, directly corresponding to the landscape sequence the section develops. | terra: The earth is spread and firm mountains are cast into it, recreating the laid plane and erected forms of the section's central tableau.

luna: The section treats the sky as a structure whose height is raised; this verse says, “وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ,” making the construction itself explicit. | terra: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا presents the sky as something built with power, an explicit nonlexical counterpart to the section's cluster of construction verbs.

luna: After the section’s cited 51:47 says the sky was built, this next ayah says the earth was spread out, joining the sky’s construction to the ground in one passage. | terra: وَٱلْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَٰهَا lays out the earth immediately after the built sky of 51:47, reproducing the upper structure and lower plane.
terra: وَٱلسَّقْفِ ٱلْمَرْفُوعِ swears by the raised roof, naming the same overhead architectural form implied when the sky is elevated.
terra: وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ joins rising or standing with glorifying the Lord in a single command to the Prophet.
terra: The Prophet is told to glorify God during the night and at the retreat of the stars, continuing 52:48's command to praise his Lord when he rises.
terra: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ restates the non-transferability of moral load, sharpening what is exceptional about a burden being removed.
terra: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ states that the final end is toward the Lord, grounding the directional force of إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ.
terra: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ joins ease directly to remembrance, the two gifts placed together in the section as eased hardship and raised dhikr.
terra: People are torn away like trunks of uprooted palms, turning an upright living form into a bodily image of removal from its base.
terra: The repeated refrain that the Quran is made easy for remembrance confirms that the ease–dhikr conjunction persists after the people of Noah's account.
terra: After Thamud's account, the same refrain again couples divine facilitation with remembrance.
terra: The fourth refrain again makes the Quran easy for remembrance, a repeated external meeting of the section's two central gifts.

luna: The section explicitly reads this verse’s two verbs together: the sky is raised and the balance placed (“رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ”), joining its paired acts of lifting and setting down in a single creation scene. | terra: He raises the sky and places the balance, رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ, putting the section's two opposed construction motions into one ordered creation.

luna: After the section’s cited 55:7 places the balance, this ayah says not to transgress in it; it supplies the first boundary for the balance image that the section names. | terra: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْمِيزَانِ gives the first purpose of the balance placed in 55:7: created order must not be transgressed.

luna: The section cites 55:7’s placed balance; this next ayah commands just weighing and forbids making the balance deficient, specifying what that placed measure does. | terra: وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ commands people to set weight upright in justice; it states how the balance placed in 55:7 must be maintained.

luna: The section identifies this as the next placed object after the raised sky and placed balance: “وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ” sets the earth for living beings. | terra: وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ makes the earth the corresponding thing laid down for living beings beneath the raised sky of 55:7.
terra: When the sky splits and becomes rose-red like oil or hide, the ordered heaven raised in 55:7 reaches its eschatological undoing in the same surah.
terra: خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ describes the Event as lowering and raising; it compresses the section's downward placement and upward elevation into a reversal of rank.
terra: When the earth is shaken violently, the stable ground of the construction image begins to come apart; 56:5–6 give the mountains' resulting dissolution.
terra: وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسًّا says the mountains are pulverized, directly reversing their installation as firm pegs.
terra: The pulverized mountains become scattered dust, completing the dismantling begun in 56:4–5.
terra: وَفُرُشٍ مَّرْفُوعَةٍ adds raised couches or beds to the Quran's furnished scenes, paralleling the raised couches of 88:13.
terra: God sends scripture and ٱلْمِيزَانَ so people may uphold justice; it states the human purpose of the balance placed in 55:7.

luna: The section’s root ر ف ع reaches beyond buildings to raised remembrance; this verse says God raises believers and those given knowledge by degrees (“يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ... دَرَجَاتٍ”), another explicit elevation of standing. | terra: God يَرْفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ... دَرَجَٰتٍ uses physical elevation for honored rank, clarifying the semantic move from raising structures to raising remembrance.
terra: يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيْدِيهِمْ depicts people dismantling their own houses, a direct built-object counterpart to the section's literal definition of نقض البناء.
terra: Palms are either cut down or left قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا, standing on their roots; the ayah explicitly places severed and upright forms across one boundary.
terra: A mountain would be خَٰشِعًا مُّتَصَدِّعًا under the Quran's descent; a received weight makes even a massive created structure crack, closely echoing the load and creaking back.
terra: Those fighting in ordered ranks are كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَٰنٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ, like a tightly joined building, applying structural integrity to upright human bodies.
terra: The term of pregnant women lasts until يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ; the legal rule rests on the same idiom of setting down one's load.
terra: Support continues حَتَّىٰ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ, again making childbirth an actual release of a carried burden.

luna: The section develops hardship alongside promised ease; this verse gives God’s promise “سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا,” the same specific transition from hardship to ease. | terra: سَيَجْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا states that God will make ease after hardship, the closest sequential parallel to the section's doubled assurance that ease accompanies hardship.
terra: Pharaoh's wife asks رَبِّ ٱبْنِ لِى عِندَكَ بَيْتًا فِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ; a prayer to the Lord for a house to be built complements Abraham and Ishmael building while praying to their Lord.

terra: The ordered heavens show no تَفَٰوُتٍ and the viewer is challenged to find فُطُورٍ, any fissure; intact cosmic construction forms the boundary opposite the section's creaking, near-broken carrier.
terra: After their garden is destroyed, its owners say إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ, exactly the stance toward the Lord commanded at the section's close.
terra: The earth and mountains are carried and crushed in one blow; raised and anchored creation becomes a borne mass that is structurally demolished.
terra: The sky is split and becomes وَاهِيَةٌ, frail; an elevated cosmic structure reaches the state of weakness implicit in the section's cracking back.
terra: People rush from graves كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ, as toward an erected marker or cult-stone, giving the root's protruding object a kinetic scene.
terra: God makes the earth بِسَاطًا, an expanse, which parallels the placed ground beneath elevated and erected forms.

luna: The section’s dictionary reading of 94:7 has the addressee stand upright after finishing; this command tells the Prophet to rise for night worship, a specific parallel in stance and divine address. | terra: قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا tells the same prophetic addressee to rise and stand at night, concretizing the devotional exertion of فَٱنصَبْ.
terra: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِى عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا promises that a weighty word will be cast upon the same prophetic addressee, a precise counter-motion to the burden taken off him.

luna: The section joins raised remembrance with longing toward the Lord; this verse commands the Prophet to remember his Lord’s name and devote himself wholly to Him, bringing those two features together in a devotional act. | terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ orders the Prophet to remember his Lord's name and devote himself wholly to Him, the closest imperative parallel to turning desire toward the Lord.
terra: ٱلسَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌۢ بِهِ makes the sky split under the promised Day, a cosmic analogue for a structure giving way under what comes upon it.

terra: The long night-standing command is lightened when God knows the believers cannot sustain its measure and allows فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ; exertion, relieved load, and ease meet in one prophetic context.
terra: قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ commands the prophetic addressee to arise for his task; 74:3 immediately directs magnification to his Lord.
terra: وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ places the Lord as the object of magnification directly after the command to rise, paralleling “stand/exert, then desire your Lord.”
terra: The denier doubts that God will gather his bones; 75:4 answers with the ability to refashion even fingertips, treating the body as a structure reassembled.
terra: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُ specifies precise bodily reconstruction, countering the section's body at the edge of coming apart.
terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ commands remembrance of the Lord's name morning and evening; 76:26 then gives its bodily worship forms.
terra: Night prostration and prolonged glorification enact the exertion commanded after remembering the Lord's name in 76:25.
terra: When the sky is fissured, the elevated cosmic structure passes from integrity to opening.
terra: God places lofty firm mountains on earth and gives sweet water, connecting raised mass with provision from the prepared world.
terra: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ مِهَٰدًا makes the earth a prepared bed, the horizontal ground for the mountain-pegs of 78:7.

luna: The section’s dictionary entry for root ع س ر gives a peg game in which an upright piece is knocked out; this verse calls mountains “أَوْتَادًا” (pegs), a related fixed-upright image whose function is the reverse: anchoring rather than removal. | terra: وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا calls mountains pegs, a direct nonlexical parallel to the section's erected stake and to the mountains نُصِبَتْ in 88:19.

luna: The section treats the sky as raised construction; this verse says seven strong structures were built above the addressees (“وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا”), a specific parallel in the same sky-building image. | terra: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا depicts the seven heavens above as strongly built, the stable cosmic structure opposite a back nearing structural failure.
terra: Of the sky, بَنَىٰهَا explicitly says God built it; 79:28 then specifies the elevation and ordering by which that cosmic construction was made.

luna: The section cites this verse for the building sense of root ر ف ع: the sky’s height is raised and proportioned (“رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا”), a direct architectural counterpart to the lifted name. | terra: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّىٰهَا raises the sky's canopy and makes it proportionate, joining elevation to structural finishing.

luna: The section cites 79:28 for the raised sky; this same creation passage then says the earth was spread out, a specific continuation from upper structure to ground. | terra: After the sky is built and raised in 79:27–28, the earth is spread out; this row contributes the lower plane that completes that construction tableau.
luna: Following the section’s 79:28 sky and this passage’s spread earth, this ayah says its water and pasture were brought forth; it adds what the earth provides in that continuing creation scene.

luna: The section’s landscape sequence includes mountains erected; this verse says the mountains were firmly set (“وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا”), a related account of their placement in the earth. | terra: وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَرْسَىٰهَا anchors the mountains after the earth is spread, giving structural fixation to the creation sequence begun with the raised sky.
terra: The honored pages are مَّرْفُوعَةٍ مُّطَهَّرَةٍ, raised and purified; elevation marks the rank of revelation rather than the position of a building.
terra: ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ says God eases the human path after creation, setting facilitation within the making of the human being.
terra: وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ depicts the sky stripped away, a different mode of dismantling the overhead structure.
terra: إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنفَطَرَتْ repeats the Quran's direct image of the built heaven splitting open.
terra: God خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ, creating, proportioning, and balancing the human; it supplies the body's sound construction behind the image of a strained back.
terra: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ says God assembled the human in the form He willed, making bodily construction explicit.
terra: إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ gives another explicit dissolution of the raised sky and immediately places it under obedience to its Lord.
terra: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ addresses the human as laboring toward his Lord, joining exertion and directed movement exactly as the section's last two commands do.
terra: سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى commands the prophetic addressee to glorify the name of his Most High Lord, bringing raised name, Lord, and directed worship into one line.
terra: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ is another direct divine promise of ease to the prophetic addressee, pairing closely with the promise that follows his lifted burden.
luna: The section moves from raised remembrance to standing and turning toward the Lord; this verse joins remembrance of the Lord’s name to prayer, a compact parallel to that pairing.
terra: عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ uses the ن ص ب family for exhausting toil in the same surah that says mountains نُصِبَتْ; it exposes the fatigue/erection ambiguity surrounding فَٱنصَبْ.
terra: Paradise contains سُرُرٌ مَّرْفُوعَةٌ, raised couches; immediately before cups are “placed” in 88:14, this restages the section's elevation and placement as a furnished interior.
terra: وَأَكْوَابٌ مَّوْضُوعَةٌ names cups deliberately placed beside the raised couches of 88:13, an exact small-scale pairing of وضع and رفع.
terra: Cushions are arrayed in rows after the raised couches and placed cups; this contributes ordered arrangement to the same paradisal construction scene.
terra: Carpets are spread out after 88:13–15, completing the arranged floor beneath the elevated and placed furnishings.

luna: The section explicitly treats the camel, sky, mountains, and earth as one scene. This ayah opens it by asking how the camel was created; 88:18–20 then carry the gaze to raised sky, erected mountains, and spread earth.

luna: This ayah asks how the sky was raised (“كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ”), the same physical elevation developed in the section; 88:19 and 88:20 complete its linked mountain-and-earth scene. | terra: The sky is asked of, كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ, beginning the creation tableau whose mountains are erected and earth spread in 88:19–20.

luna: This is the section’s explicit example of root ن ص ب applied to mountains: “كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ,” set up as projecting objects, extending the image from the upright stake to a landscape. | terra: The mountains are asked of, كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ; this is the section's exact Quranic scene of massive objects set upright.

luna: The section names this as the earth’s counterpart after raised sky and erected mountains; the ayah asks how the earth was spread (“كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ”), completing that vertical-to-ground scene. | terra: The spread earth completes 88:18–19's raised-sky and erected-mountain construction, supplying the laid-out plane beneath the elevated forms.
terra: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلْعِمَادِ identifies Iram by its pillars, placing monumental upright supports in the passage that later names Pharaoh's stakes.
terra: Thamud carve rock in the valley, turning the mountain material itself into durable human construction.
terra: وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِى ٱلْأَوْتَادِ repeats Pharaoh's association with stakes in a passage about monumental peoples, keeping the peg within an architectural-power setting.
terra: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا بَنَىٰهَا swears by the sky and its Builder, reinforcing the section's reading of creation through building acts.
terra: وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا طَحَىٰهَا pairs the built sky of 91:5 with earth spread beneath it, another upper-structure/lower-plane scene.
terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ promises facilitation toward ease for the giver who fears and affirms the best.
terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ reverses 92:7 by facilitating the miser toward hardship, showing that “making easy” can lead toward a hard end.
terra: Humanity is created فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ, in the best upright constitution; bodily form is presented as something set straight before the reversal in 95:5.
terra: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَٰهُ أَسْفَلَ سَٰفِلِينَ reverses the upright human formation of 95:4 by returning it to the lowest state, illuminating the section's elevation and lowering axis.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ makes return to the Lord the endpoint, another concise statement of the section's final orientation.
terra: وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب commands prostration and approach, another concise bodily orientation toward the Lord after opposition.
terra: The fire closes over them فِى عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍ, in extended columns; this may recall erected supports, though the image's exact spatial arrangement is uncertain.
terra: A rope مِن مَّسَدٍ is around the woman's neck; the tightly twisted cord becomes a bodily load, bringing together rope-making and burden-bearing without the unravelling act.
terra: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ establishes the Lord to whom refuge is directed; 113:4 supplies the knots that make the source's رب–knot association specific.

terra: The refuge sought from the Lord in 113:1 includes protection from ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ, blowers in knots; Lord and knots meet in one short surah, matching the source dictionary's ر ب ب knot association.
